KEY MESSAGE 1...
High pressure continues to shift east of New England this 
afternoon. A mid and upper level ridge will continue to 
influence the sensible weather through tonight, as low pressure 
will organize near the NC Coast overnight. After mild temps in 
the 50s to lower and spotty mid 60s this afternoon, expect lows
to drop off into the 30s to lower 40s. The winds will go light 
to calm in the sheltered valleys with mostly clear to partly 
cloudy skies early on before higher clouds increase and it 
becomes mostly cloudy. Some radiational cooling will occur with 
lows potentially in the lower to mid 30s over the southern 
Dacks, and the Upper Hudson Valley, Lake George/Glens Falls 
area and southern VT. We blended the NBM/MAV MOS mins for lows 
tonight.

Tomorrow, the extended stretch of dry weather will end by the
afternoon. Clouds will be thickening and lowering from south to
north, as the coastal low approaches. PWATs increase to 1 to 2+
STDEVs above normal, as an inverted sfc trough north of the fast
moving wave approaches from the Delmarva Region will initially 
bring some rain into the region. The cold front will be well to 
the west over the Great Lakes Region and Midwest, so in the fast
southwest flow aloft the coastal wave will impact the region 
especially from the Capital Region, southern VT and the northern
and eastern Catskills south and east. The best low to mid level
FGEN looks like to will be near the extreme southeast portion 
of the forecast area and over central/southern New England. 
There is some support from the right entrance region of the 
upper level jet north and east of the region, as the isentropic 
lift and moisture advection increase Sun early evening. However,
the latest guidance including the RRFS, GFS, ECMWF and the NBM 
have shifted further east with the coastal wave. The 12Z 3-km 
HRRR was the furthest west taking the low over NYC. The 12Z EC 
is the furthest east with the least amount of rainfall. Most of 
the other guidance is also east over eastern Long Island or 
southeast New England/Cape Cod. Its a very compact wave and 
their will be a sharp cutoff with the rainfall. Our latest 
QPF/rainfall forecasts supports a blend of the NBM/latest WPC 
amounts. The rainfall should end quickly between 06Z-12Z/Mon. 

The latest 13Z NBM 24-hr probabilities for >0.50" of rainfall 
are 50-80% for the period ending 12Z/Mon from Albany south and 
east into the mid Hudson Valley, southern and central Taconics, 
Berkshires and Litchfield County CT. The 13Z NBM probs >1" of
rainfall are 40-55% for portions of the mid Hudson Valley,
southern Taconics, Litchfield County,CT and the extreme southern
Berkshires. Our latest forecast had about a tenth of an inch to
a quarter inch for locations north and west of the Capital
Region/southern VT. Around a half an inch to inch south and 
east of the eastern Capital District and southern VT with the 
best chance of an inch to inch and a quarter over Litchfield 
County, CT. The lower rainfall amounts, high gridded FFG values 
(1.8-2.5"/3 hours), and the fast moving wave will reduce any 
isolated flash flood threat (WPC has the Berkshires, mid-Hudson 
Valley, southern Taconics, and NW CT in a Marginal Risk in the 
current ERO). The rain will be beneficial with the recent dry 
stretch over the past week. Temps on Sunday will continue to be
in the mid 50s to lower 60s with a few cooler spots over the 
northern mtns. Expect lows Sun night to be mid in the 40s to 
lower 50s with the cold front still to the west. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...A strong cold front will move across the region
on Monday with limited low-level moisture associated with it. A
few light showers may reach the southwest Adirondacks.
Otherwise, max temps may peak in the late morning/early pm. A 
much colder air mass will move into the region. We continued to 
increase winds Mon pm into early Mon night, as W/NW winds 
increase to 10-15 mph with some gusts 20-35 mph. The strongest 
gusts will be in the Capital Region into the Berkshires. The 
strong cold advection continues into Monday night with H850 
temps falling to -8C to -12C. A few lake effect showers or 
flurries may impact the western Mohawk Valley and western 
Adirondacks. Any accumulation looks very light. Lows fall into 
the 20s to lower 30s in the brisk conditions. Highs on Tuesday 
will be 5 or more degrees colder than normal with 30s to lower 
40s. Some locations in the southern Dacks and southern Greens 
may not get out of the 20s. High pressure builds in late Tue 
into Wed with fair, dry and cold weather. 

Late Wed night into Thanksgiving...A broad upper level trough
develops east of the MS River River Valley over the eastern
CONUS. Multiple short-waves will be moving through the trough 
with the potential for a coastal low or a double barrel low 
pressure system impacting the region Thanksgiving/Thanksgiving 
night into Fri/Sat. The forecast confidence is very low and
